name: Search SMS logs
description: Call this when you need the per-message SMS sending history for an account over a date range — the individual transactional SMS events behind the Logs screen, paged. This is a search that happens to be expressed as a POST: the criteria travel in the body. Use it to answer "was this SMS delivered", "what went out last week", or to page through recent sends. It reads only; to send an SMS or to inspect aggregate SMS statistics rather than individual log rows, use the corresponding send or statistics action instead. Note that the response envelope reports totalCount, so a first call with a small limit is the cheap way to size a range before paging it.
preconditions: The session must be authenticated against the transactional SMS backend (transactional-app-backend-sms.brevo.com).
The account must have transactional SMS available for any log rows to exist; an account that has never sent SMS returns an empty data array.

startDate.description: Inclusive start of the window to search, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. "2026-10-30T03:00:00.000Z". Observed as the start of a 7-day window.

endDate.description: Inclusive end of the window to search, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. "2026-11-06T18:19:50.026Z". Observed set to the moment of the request.

limit.description: Maximum number of log rows to return in this page. Observed as 20; no maximum is documented, so do not assume one above what you have seen.

page.description: 1-based page number within the result set. Observed as 1.

data.description: The SMS log rows for the requested page. Empty when the account has no SMS activity in the window. The per-row field shape was not observed — only an empty array was seen — so do not assume field names.

skip.description: Number of rows skipped before this page, derived from page and limit.

limit.description: The page size echoed back from the request.

page.description: The page number echoed back from the request.

totalCount.description: Total number of log rows matching the date range across all pages.

side_effects: None observed: the call returns SMS log rows and does not alter account data. It is a POST only because the search criteria are sent in the body, and it answers 201 rather than 200.
